label: Organic Law 3/2021 on euthanasia (LORE)
description: Spain's right to die since 2021: administration by the care team or self-administration. Pentobarbital sits at its margins, reserved for the rare oral route.

label: Ministry recommendations on medicines for the procedure
description: Pentobarbital, prepared as a compounded oral solution, is the drug of choice for self-administration; secobarbital is the alternative. If both run short, the procedure switches to the intravenous route.

label: Catalan dispensing order and protocol
description: For oral self-administration in Catalonia, the dispensing pharmacy is always Vall d'Hebron. Preparation, storage and dispensing follow a pharmacological protocol of the Servei Català de la Salut.

label: Evaluation commissions
description: Regional guarantee and evaluation commissions approve each request before death. One in three applicants dies before a decision; 97 people died after approval in 2025.

label: Supreme Court ruling on standing (May 2026)
description: People with a particularly close bond to the applicant may challenge an approved euthanasia in court. A minority warned it turns the right into a right to a bad death.

label: Assisted dying statistics
description: 565 assisted deaths in 2025, 1,668 since 2021. Catalonia leads requests (6.14 per 100,000), then Navarra (5.41). Provisional: the full report will revise them.

label: AEMPS
description: Authorises veterinary pentobarbital products and issued safety notes in December 2023 and February 2026 after scavenger poisonings, mostly in Asturias and Navarra.

label: Law 7/2023 on animal welfare
description: In force since September 2023. Bans killing companion animals for space or economic reasons; euthanasia only by a vet, when welfare is compromised. Spain's second 'good death' law in two years.

label: Royal Decree 1632/2011 on scavenger feeding
description: After the BSE crisis banned leaving carcasses in the field, this decree lets regions delimit feeding zones for scavenger species where livestock carcasses may stay.

label: Animal by-products rules
description: Dead pets are Category 1, the highest-risk class: incineration, authorised cemeteries or research. Burial varies by region, from private gardens in Galicia to inaccessible areas only in Asturias.
verification_note: The rules say where the body goes, not the drug.

label: Navarra regional police (Baztán)
description: In March 2024 found six dead griffon vultures around cattle carcasses in a protected feeding zone; birds and carcasses tested positive. A criminal investigation followed.

label: MITECO feeding-zone reports
description: In 2022 and 2023 at least ten regions authorised extensive farms to leave carcasses for scavengers without removal.

label: Moehs Ibérica (Rubí)
description: Head of a group producing active pharmaceutical ingredients since 1962; listed among pentobarbital sodium suppliers.
verification_note: A listing does not say where the molecule is made.

label: Labiana Life Sciences (Terrassa)
description: Releases batches of the veterinary product Eutanax, and of Allfatal vet. for Sweden: pentobarbital leaves the Vallès for Scandinavia.

label: Fatro Ibérica (Sant Just Desvern)
description: Holds the authorisation of Eutanax, authorised since 1992. Its leaflet warns that carcasses must never be eaten by other animals.

label: Vall d'Hebron hospital pharmacy
description: Compounds and dispenses every oral dose for assisted dying in Catalonia.

label: Valdecilla hospital pharmacy
description: Centralises compounding for Cantabria; two other hospitals request doses in advance.
source: Servicio Cántabro de Salud, form E10

label: Hospital pharmacists
description: In a 2023 survey, 81% knew the law and 63% would not object. Between prescription and glass, as in Switzerland.

label: The compounded oral solution
description: The human drug is handmade, dose by dose, for a route almost nobody chooses: 18 people in 2023. The only route where the person takes it with their own hand.

label: Intravenous procedure
description: How most Spanish assisted deaths happen, administered by the care team without pentobarbital. A right to die built around the procedure, not the drug.

label: Veterinarians
description: The only people allowed to administer pentobarbital to animals: in clinics, shelters, stables and farms.

label: Shelters under 'sacrificio cero'
description: Killing healthy shelter animals, put at around 100,000 a year, ended with Law 7/2023. Euthanasia now needs a vet's justification.

label: Laboratory animals
description: Rodents in research are routinely euthanised with pentobarbital; the Ministry of Agriculture publishes annual figures on animals used.

label: The euthanised carcass
description: Where Spain's case turns. The drug outlives the animal it killed: still active in muscle and viscera, it poisons whatever eats the dead. One documented case: dogs poisoned by a horse euthanised two years earlier.

label: Feeding zones for scavengers
description: Conservation infrastructure where livestock carcasses are left on purpose. A euthanised cow placed there turns care for scavengers into a delivery system for the drug.

label: Griffon vultures
description: Pentobarbital in 93.3% of barbiturate intoxications in Spanish wildlife (2004 to 2020); griffon vultures most affected, two thirds of cases in Navarra.

label: Bearded vulture case
description: Found electrocuted with pentobarbital in stomach and liver; the drug may have impaired its balance before it hit the cables.
verification_note: Location within northern Spain not confirmed.

label: Soil and water
description: The slowest afterlife. Abroad, pentobarbital has persisted in groundwater for decades, in soils for months and in compost for over a year.
verification_note: No Spanish study of soil or water found.

label: Rendering and incineration
description: Where most carcasses should go. In the US, residues reached pet food through rendered tallow; how Spain checks this is open.

label: Pet cemeteries and private burial
description: A growing sector, plus regional permissions to bury pets at home. Mourning, care and residue in the same patch of soil.

label: Derecho a Morir Dignamente (DMD)
description: The right-to-die association: five-year report on the LORE, campaigns for dedicated euthanasia units in every region.

label: Abogados Cristianos
description: Catholic lawyers' association that backed families' suits to stop approved euthanasias.

label: Noelia Castillo case
description: A 25-year-old Barcelona woman whose euthanasia was suspended the day before it was due in 2024, at her father's request. Through five courts and the ECHR; she died in March 2026.

label: Francesc Augé case
description: A 55-year-old Barcelona man suspended by his father's appeal; the case produced the Supreme Court's 2026 ruling on standing before the father withdrew.

label: Illicit online offers
description: A Telegram contact offering lethal doses from another European country, reported in June 2026. Recorded only as discourse.

label: SEO/BirdLife
description: Conservationists who lobbied to restore carcasses for scavengers after the BSE ban.

label: Herrero-Villar et al. 2021
description: Increasing barbiturate intoxication in avian scavengers in Spain, 2004 to 2020.

label: Payne et al. 2015
description: Pentobarbital residues in equine compost piles over 367 days.

label: Peschka et al.
description: Barbiturates in German rivers and groundwater, decades after infiltration.

label: O.F.I.L. 2023 survey
description: Hospital pharmacists' knowledge of the euthanasia law and conscientious objection.

label: Orrego, Toxic Afterlives (forthcoming)
description: Specimenography and the uneven residues of industrial farming: the method for following what the drug leaves behind.

label: MORTALMED
description: ERC project led by Marcos Freire de Andrade Neves. A Spanish fieldsite is a possibility the PI mentioned, conditional on ERC approval; this map is a thinking device, not a proposal.
